liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the tightest version of the song they have ever heard [10]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Identified as the pick of the litter in the first set [11]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Beautifully sung but painful to hear due to missed cues and notes [14]
- **Friend of the Devil** (1 review): Described as sweet and reggaeish in this recording [15]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Considered one of the top five versions of the song ever recorded [17]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Called the best version of the song the reviewer has ever heard [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1976-06-15.143119.sbd.betty.dalton.clugston.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd76-06-15.sbd.kempa.241.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 176 min; rated 4.63/5 by 19 [4]. Said about its sound: Sound is real nice, though cuts are annoying and stretch is audible; Sound is described as crystal clear, with a sizzling Let It Grow [12][15]
- **gd76-06-15.sbd.bertha-ashley.8732.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 178 min; rated 4.64/5 by 14 [5]. Said about its sound: Bass sounds distorted, but the overall show is considered worthy of a download [13]
- **gd1976-06-15.sbd.cantor.gmb.96088.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 179 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [6]
- **gd1976-06-15.sbd.unknown.8323.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [7]

## Around the show

- A drummer's doubletime highhat reportedly throws Jerry off during the performance [14]
- Jerry's tight playing feeds the rest of the band throughout the show [18]
- Garcia's playing in 1976 is called outstanding, reflecting the band's unique energy that year [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1976-06-15.143119.sbd.betty.dalton.clugston.miller.flac1644**: taped by Betty Cantor and Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Betty's 7" two track Master Soundboard Reels @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM (16-bit/44.1k) [1]. Also: Dave Minor, Dale Shepherd, and Matt Vernon provided a Sony ECM 99A source [1]
- **gd76-06-15.sbd.kempa.241.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd76-06-15.sbd.bertha-ashley.8732.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]
- **gd1976-06-15.sbd.cantor.gmb.96088.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Bill Koucky; source: Betty Cantor 7" two track reel w/DBX-1 @ 7 1/2 ips> PCM501ES @ 44.055 kHz PCM501ES analog out>DBX-1 decoder> analog in PCM501ES analog out>Dat @ 48 kHz [6]. Also: Dropouts from reel changes were patched or edited out, with some abrupt transitions [6]
- **gd1976-06-15.sbd.unknown.8323.shnf**: source: SBD>DAT(s)>Tascam DA-20MKII>WaveTerminal 2596>CDWave>SHN [7]. Also: Beginning of Saint Stephen is clipped, with splices in Might As Well and FOTD [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Tim O'Shea: [The Dead Peak at the Beacon For The Last Time: June 15, 1976](https://nysmusic.com/2020/07/26/jerry-sundays-grateful-dead-beacon-theatre/) [25]
- Poster by Tim O'Shea: [The Dead Peak at the Beacon For The Last Time: June 15, 1976](https://nysmusic.com/2020/07/26/jerry-sundays-grateful-dead-beacon-theatre/) [26]
